correctness.rationale: Let irrational p in (0,1), beta=p/(1-p), and D(w)=beta|w|_0-|w|_1. Every tested nonempty prefix discrepancy is nonzero, because beta is irrational for any prefix containing zero, while an all-one prefix has negative integer discrepancy. After any admissible prefix append its forced ones if needed, then free zeros and floor(d)+1 ones to produce e in (-1,0). Adding m zeros and floor(e+beta m)+1 ones yields e_m={e+beta*m}-1 dense in (-1,0) by irrational rotation, and every forced transition is legal. An admissible target prefix starting zero can be inserted after the closing one with e_m close to 0-, while a target starting one can overlap the closing one with e_m close to -1+; in either case all finite strict sign tests survive a small constant offset. By Reyes Lemma 2.7 the language consists of factors of admissible prefixes, so arbitrary u,v concatenate with an admissible bridge. No mixing or specification is claimed. The logical edge cases of one-letter target and last-one forced transition are handled; a finite checker is only corroboration.

value.rationale: The irrational set is the uncountable parameter regime left open by the rational transitivity/nontransitivity classifications. An explicit dense-restart construction proves a global topological property for every irrational critical density, including very poorly approximable parameters. It is structurally distinct from finite rational discrepancy graphs, and does not claim unjustified uniform bridge bounds.
